what_office_does.text: The lieutenant governor takes over the governor’s duties when needed, including when the governor is out of state, and leads the State Senate with a tie-breaking vote. The office also chairs the Commission for Economic Development and serves on state lands, ocean protection, and university boards.
what_office_does.label: fact

candidates.name: Fiona Ma

says.text: Ma says she wants a more affordable California while keeping its economy strong, and identifies permitting delays as barriers to housing and business investment.
says.label: value

says.text: Ma says she would make higher education more affordable, expand paid internships, and strengthen pathways into careers.
says.label: value
says.quote: As Lieutenant Governor, I will make higher education more affordable, expand paid internships, and strengthen career pathways.

says.text: Ma says that as state treasurer she financed affordable housing, expanded first-time homebuyer assistance, saved distressed hospitals, and attracted job-creating investment.
says.label: fact

candidates.headline: Ma says she would work to make California more affordable while keeping its economy strong.
candidates.core_case: Ma presents her accounting background and her stated work financing housing and supporting hospitals as preparation to tackle affordability. She proposes lower-cost higher education, more paid internships, and stronger career pathways.

candidates.name: Gloria Romero

says.text: Romero says she would restore education standards, defend Title IX for girls and women in sports, and fight antisemitism on college campuses.
says.label: value

says.text: Romero says she would develop an economic plan to help businesses thrive, and identifies government bureaucracy and waste as problems.
says.label: value

says.text: Romero says she would rein in commissions, with a focus on protecting California’s water, farmland, and way of life.
says.label: value

candidates.headline: Romero says she would restore education standards.
candidates.core_case: Romero points to her service as Senate Majority Leader and her stated work on school choice and government transparency as preparation for reform. She proposes stronger education standards, support for businesses, and changes to commissions overseeing natural resources.

where_they_differ.text: Ma emphasizes affordability through housing finance, higher education, and career opportunities. Romero emphasizes education standards, school choice, campus protections, and changing how state commissions operate; both express support for business growth.
